leads.work: Manual monthly reconciliation of the full-month position (scheduled vs. actual volumes by nomination and meter). Daren Farmer sends the whole HPL position to the team, and each person has to pick out their own meters by hand and confirm back to him by a deadline (close of business Thursday).
leads.why: The message is titled 'Full month position', which suggests a recurring month-end job. It has about 3,600 nomination rows with SCHEDULED/ACTUAL/VARIANCE/STATUS/METER columns. Recipients are asked to 'pull your own meters out of this and confirm back to me', which is manual filtering and confirming that could be automated: split the report by meter owner and flag variances. Many rows show large variances and PENDING status, which may each need follow-up.

leads.work: Workaround when report attachments fail: large position spreadsheets get pasted into the email body because the attachment 'keeps bouncing off the gateway'.
leads.why: The phrase 'keeps bouncing' suggests the failure has happened more than once. It costs repeated send attempts, and pasting the data makes it harder to filter or reuse. A shared report location or report system would remove the email handoff altogether.

leads.work: Data quality checks on the scheduling/position report. FLOW_DATE values in a 'full month' report cover all of 2001 in day/month format, and counterparty IDs repeat (TXU-0000 to TXU-0399 cycle over and over).
leads.why: A month-end position that spans dates across the whole year suggests the extract is wrong or unfiltered. Each recipient would then have to clean or check the data by hand before confirming. Investigators should look for other messages about bad position or nomination reports from the same group (Farmer, Giron, Williams, Lokay).
